proposal.title: Cheaper atomic string cells
proposal.summary: Proposes cheaper atomic string cells for a later perf packet: by default built-in types from a table and no second validation of validated text, with cell reuse and a typed-value memo left for later.

body.p: (, perf-11; for a later perf packet owning src/xdm_atomic.c and src/xdm.c): (1) resolve the built-in atomic types in sxml_atomic_item_make from a table instead of describing them through the registry (measured: SchXslt expand -1.0 %); (2) let a caller that already holds validated text, such as a tree's content (tree.h: trees hold well-formed UTF-8), pass its codepoint count or skip the second validation (2.5 % of expand); (3) small-cell reuse in the item heap, kept out of the live counts only if the tests' leak checks are redefined (cells 4.3 % plus frees); (4) a typed-value memo per evaluation for untyped nodes, which needs the dynamic context to reach src/xdm_node.c.

Proposed default: the perf packet does (1) and (2), which stay inside those two files and save about 3.5 % of expand together. (3) and (4) wait: (3) changes what the tests' leak checks count, and (4) needs node atomization to reach the dynamic context, which the public sxml_node_value_request cannot carry (, ).
